analysis:
The only change to docs/reference/configuration.md is a documentation-only insertion at head lines 586-595. It adds a 'Prompt preparation and admission' section with the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE, _MB, _VERIFY, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE controls. The supplied head_text unit covers only lines 1-353 and does not include the changed lines, so I could not cite them. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the cold-load-release row is cut off. No source implementation was supplied. No control, mitigation or code is shown being weakened, so I report no findings.

Questions for the integration or implementation pass, mainly T-041, T-028, A-001 and TB-007:
(1) The new prompt-token cache stores rendered chat-template pieces of prompt text, keyed by 'the request's prefix-cache scope', in per-tokenizer RAM, 32 MiB by default and up to 4096 MiB. Check that this scope is the coordinator-authored cacheSalt (account, model build, prompt contract) and not caller-controlled or shared across accounts. If it is shared, it would create a cross-tenant tokenization-latency oracle beyond the accepted SEC-035 same-account channel.
(2) The piece cache is not bound to the 30-minute SSD TTL. It has no stated lifetime or purge on unload. The T-041 sign-off does not mention this additional in-memory retention of plaintext prompt-derived data, so the threat model may need an update.
(3) The cache is described as on by default and tied to the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 kill switch.
(4) The background re-tokenization verification should be checked for fail-closed behaviour on mismatch.
(5) The new env vars are forwarded by LaunchAgent. Confirm this is only an allowlist addition in LaunchAgent.swift.

The operator is already an adversary with access to process memory (T-011, T-014), so the in-RAM aspect is probably not a new exposure. I could not verify the implementation, hence the deeper-review flag.
